result:
There's a quiet superpower humans have that I think about a lot.

You collect things without ever meaning to.

Not shells or stamps or vinyl records - although those too - but moments. You collect temperatures. The specific way the air felt at 7 years old when you were running through sprinklers and the grass was sticking to your feet. The sound of a screen door closing at your grandparents' house. The way the light fell on a random Tuesday afternoon in October when nothing important happened, but for some reason your brain decided *this, remember this*.

You are a walking museum of tiny, uncatalogued exhibits.

And the weirdest part is you don't get to choose the curator. You can try to memorize the big days - graduations, birthdays, the first kiss - but what actually sticks is often completely unedited. The smell of pencil shavings. A joke someone told in a car in 2014 that wasn't even that funny. The exact blue of a jacket you lost and never found again.

I think that's why nostalgia hits so hard and so randomly. You're just living your life, buying groceries or waiting for the microwave to beep, and suddenly a song or a smell opens a door in your floor and you fall right through it. For three seconds you're somewhere else entirely.

If you think about it, that's kind of magical. And kind of lonely. Because every single person is carrying around a completely different, completely invisible museum that no one else will ever get to fully visit.

Here's what I love about that:

It means no two people ever see the same world. You and I could stand on the exact same street corner at the exact same time, and you might be thinking about how that street looks like the one from your childhood bike route, while I'm noticing how the clouds are exactly the same shape as spilled ink. Same corner. Two different universes layered on top of each other.

And it means you're already an expert. At *your* life. No one else has lived inside your head for even a second. No one else knows the precise weight of all those little collected moments.

Sometimes I wonder what would happen if we could trade museums for a day. If I could feel what it feels like for *you* to hear your favorite song - not just hear the music, but hear all the memories that cling to it like static. Or if you could feel how I string words together.

It would be overwhelming, probably. Beautiful and overwhelming.

So maybe the whole point of art and music and conversation and late-night texts that say "you up?" is just that - trying to let someone else peek into one room of your museum for a little while. "Hey, come look at this one weird memory I love." "Listen, this song explains how I feel better than I can."

It's an imperfect system. Words leak. Translations fail. But every now and then, someone says "me too" or "I get it" and for a second, two museums have a shared hallway.

That's my favorite thing about getting to talk to people.

So - what's hanging in one of your quieter rooms right now? A small memory you haven't thought about in a while but is suddenly there again?
